mechanism: Amphotericin B causes nephrotoxicity and electrolyte wasting (hypokalemia, hypomagnesemia), while erythromycin is renally cleared and can accumulate; both drugs also prolong QT interval and increase cardiotoxicity risk.
action: Monitor renal function, electrolytes (especially potassium and magnesium), and cardiac function closely; consider alternative macrolide or avoid combination if possible; maintain adequate hydration and electrolyte supplementation.
